newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on exports, harvest slowdown.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on exports, harvest slowdown.

text.p: Active exports and a slowdown in corn harvesting in the eastern U.S. growing region boosted CBOT corn futures to a higher close, traders said.
"Week after week we continue to get good sales and with the report out Tuesday we may get more people covering shorts," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA Thursday said U.S. corn net exports for the week ended October 31 were at 860,200 tonnes, above expectations for 500,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
Private forecasts this week for less corn to produced this year in the U.S. than previously were supportive.
Closely-followed analytical firm Sparks Companies Wednesday projected corn production would total 9.147 billion bushels. The market was expecting 9.2 billion to 9.3 billion.
In a Reuter survey this week, an average of analysts' estimates pegged the corn crop at 9.145 billion bushels.

Refco Inc bought eight millin bushels of March, ADM Investor Services sold three million March and Continental Grain sold two million March. The Chicago Corp also sold four million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn closed 1/2 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 4-1/2 at $2.64-1/2 a bushel.
Technical indicators showed corn was oversold and due for a bounce.
The nine day daily relative strength index (RSI) for December closed Wednesday at 17 points, below the oversold area of 30. The RSI Thursday closed at 32 points.
First resistance in the December was at $2.61-1/2 a bushel and second resistance at $2.64-1/4. The session high for December was $2.66.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 65,000 contracts, down from 80,963 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
The Chicago Corp bought 300 March $2.90 calls at 4-1/2 cents and LIT America bought 500 December $2.70 calls, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 28,000 contracts, down from 31,264 Wednesday.
